newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China seen handling 3 mln tonnes aircargo by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China seen handling 3 mln tonnes aircargo by 2000.

text.p: Chinese airports were predicted to handle about three million tonnes of air cargo per annum by the year 2000, double that recorded in 1995, a Chinese airline executive was quoted as saying.

The semi-official China News Service (CNS) quoted China International Airlines deputy cargo service manager Zhang Kehan as saying just in China's three major hubs of Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou 250,000 tonnes of air cargo were handled in 1995.
Zhang said Chinese airlines handled 2.23 billion tonne-kilometres of airfreight by the end of 1995, rising at an annual growth rate of 20.8 percent.
The 1995 figure was 870 percent over that of 1983, he said.
While China handled hardly any international cargo services in the 1980s, last year some 56.7 percent of China's air cargo deliveries were international, Zhang said.
